finding_13_001_grammar.resolution: Eliminated contradictory regex patterns. Enforced unified canonical lexical grammar across all 7 kinds. Disallowed hyphens to prevent CLI/casing ambiguity and align with active Capability Registry. Defined deterministic 8-step validator execution order.

finding_13_002_ownership.resolution: Separated entity kinds from root ownership namespaces. Established closed root taxonomy [core, gov, sys, pack, ext, integration]. Enforced third-party isolation strictly under ext.* (no unreserved root squatting). Eliminated invalid synthesis.* reference in favor of core.*. Enforced module scope boundary invariant.

finding_13_003_safety_and_kinds.resolution: Standardized canonical kind name settings (plural, matching roadmap). Defined explicit disambiguation via kind discriminator tuple {kind, id}. Defined strict immutability and 3-stage lifecycle [ACTIVE, DEPRECATED, RETIRED]. Clarified Step 13 scope boundaries and non-conflict with existing governance Capability Registry.

canonical_lexical_grammar.casing_enforcement: strict lowercase ASCII; reject fail-closed on uppercase (no silent normalization)
validator_execution_order: 1. PRIMITIVE_CHECK: verify input is non-null string
2. CHARACTER_SET_SCREENING: verify all characters match [a-z0-9_.] (fail on uppercase, hyphens, spaces, symbols)
4. STRUCTURAL_DOT_CHECK: verify string does not start with ., end with ., or contain ..
5. SEGMENT_EXTRACTION: split string by . delimiter into segments array
7. SEGMENT_LENGTH_CHECK: verify each segment has 1 <= segment.length <= 48
canonical_lexical_grammar.kind_uniformity: Lexical grammar is identical for all 7 kinds. Semantic rules (such as root ownership) are evaluated at the semantic validation layer.

root_segment_taxonomy.core: core.* — Core framework, first-party foundation subsystems, installer, official first-party modules (min 2 segments, e.g. core.database.postgresql, core.installer)
root_segment_taxonomy.gov: gov.* — Formal governance framework, contracts, capsules, seals, attestations (min 2 segments, e.g. gov.capsule.persistence)
root_segment_taxonomy.sys: sys.* — Host runtime, OS abstraction, kernel process runtime internals (min 2 segments, e.g. sys.process.signal)
root_segment_taxonomy.pack: pack.* — Project Packs (min 3 segments, e.g. pack.starter.setup)
root_segment_taxonomy.ext: ext.* — Third-party modules and external vendor extensions (min 3 segments, e.g. ext.acme.blog.post.created; all third-party code strictly isolated under ext.*)
root_segment_taxonomy.integration: integration.* — First-party integration adapters and external provider connectors (min 2 segments, e.g. integration.storage.s3, integration.payment.stripe)

forbidden_root_operations: NO_UNRESERVED_ROOT: No entity may register a root segment outside [core, gov, sys, pack, ext, integration]
NO_VENDOR_ROOT_SQUATTING: Third parties cannot claim top-level namespace roots; must be under ext.<publisher_id>.<module_id>.*
NO_SYNTHESIS_ROOT: Legacy synthesis.* namespace forbidden in mini; all first-party code belongs to core.*
NO_KIND_AS_ROOT: Entity kinds (permission, event, etc.) cannot be used as root ownership segments
namespace_ownership_model.module_scope_boundary_invariant: Every module has a canonical module identifier of kind module (e.g. ext.acme.blog). All capabilities, permissions, events, and settings registered by that module MUST be prefixed by the module identifier (ext.acme.blog.*). Modules cannot declare identifiers outside their assigned namespace.

capability.description: Features or interfaces provided or required by Core or Modules

permission.description: Authorization tokens for server-side RBAC and access control gates

event.description: Domain and lifecycle event topics dispatched across event bus

settings.description: Configuration keys for Core, Modules, and Themes (canonical plural: settings)

module.description: Packaging identifiers for first-party and third-party modules

entitlement.description: Commercial licensing and feature gate tokens (strictly isolated from permissions)

integration.description: External provider and adapter connection identifiers

registry_safety_invariants: INV-NAMESPACE-UNIQUE: No duplicate identifier allowed within any given kind registry domain.
INV-NAMESPACE-DISAMBIGUATION: Identifiers are strictly evaluated as a tuple {kind, id}. An event cannot be evaluated as a permission.
INV-NAMESPACE-OWNERSHIP: Third-party entities cannot declare identifiers in reserved core.*, gov.*, sys.* namespaces. Must reside in ext.<publisher_id>.<module_id>.*.
INV-NAMESPACE-IMMUTABLE: Published stable identifiers are permanently immutable; cannot be renamed, repurposed, or deleted without formal contract supersession.

INV-NAMESPACE-LIFECYCLE: Identifiers follow state machine ACTIVE -> DEPRECATED -> RETIRED. Deprecated identifiers remain functional but trigger warnings; retired identifiers reject usage and prevent name reuse.
INV-NAMESPACE-FAIL-CLOSED: Unknown, unregistered, or syntactically invalid identifiers evaluate to REJECT/DENY by default.
INV-NAMESPACE-NO-WILDCARD-INHERITANCE: Authorization permissions do not grant wildcard sub-permissions by prefix matching; exact matching required.
INV-NAMESPACE-SEPARATION: Permissions (access control) and Entitlements (licensing) are strictly separated types with no cross-inheritance.

positive_cases: Valid core.* and gov.* identifiers under reserved roots
Identifiers containing underscores within segments (e.g. core.multi_tenant)
negative_cases: Uppercase ASCII characters (reject fail-closed, no auto-lowercase)
Leading dots, trailing dots, consecutive dots (..)

Third party attempting to declare root namespace outside ext.*
Module attempting to declare identifier outside its module prefix
